description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation to support regulated customers adopting Dedicated and Private deployments. The “Retention controls + compliance reporting pack” project delivers (1) productized retention configuration across key data classes (request/response logs, prompts/completions where stored, audit logs, traces/metrics, artifacts like eval datasets where applicable) and (2) a baseline compliance report package that can be generated on-demand for customers and internal audits.

Goals:
- Ship customer-configurable retention controls with safe defaults by tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and clear behavior (TTL, purge semantics, legal hold, and exceptions).
- Provide a baseline compliance reporting pack: audit-log coverage summary, retention configuration export, data residency/region summary, access control/RBAC report, and evidence collection checklist aligned to SOC 2/ISO-style controls.
- Reduce sales/CS overhead during security reviews by standardizing responses and artifacts (Security FAQ, customer-ready report templates, and repeatable evidence procedure).

Scope:
- Control plane support for retention policies (schema, API endpoints, validation, change history, and policy evaluation).
- Data plane/telemetry integrations to enforce retention (scheduled deletion jobs, backfills, and verification metrics).
- Audit log exporter enhancements to support report generation and time-windowed exports.
- Console surfaces and docs updates (where applicable) to view/edit retention settings and download reports.

Non-goals (initial release):
- Full custom report builder; advanced “bring your own GRC” integrations beyond export formats.
- Arbitrary per-field redaction policies (handled separately under logging standards).

Key stakeholders:
- Security & Compliance: Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO), Marcus Lin (SecEng), Olga Petrov (GRC), Kevin Osei (retention/audit exports).
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Dir PM Security & Compliance).
- Engineering (Platform/Control Plane): Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee.
- Telemetry/Observability: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson.
- SRE/Infra: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant (operational guardrails, runbooks, verification).
- GTM enablement: sales engineering + customer success for packaging and customer-facing collateral.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements, data inventory, and policy schema draft.
- Phase 1 (3–5 weeks): implement retention policy service + APIs, initial purge jobs for core stores, telemetry verification.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): compliance report pack MVP (exports + dashboards), customer-facing docs + enablement.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): staged rollout (internal, design partners), hardening, and GA criteria.

Constraints and risks:
- Must avoid performance regressions in telemetry pipelines and ensure purges are idempotent and observable.
- Must ensure retention settings do not conflict with incident response needs (e.g., short-lived logs vs. on-call debugging) via break-glass and documented exceptions.
- Must align terminology with legal/compliance expectations (data classes, “audit logs” vs. “request logs”, and legal hold semantics).
